# Offline provider/controller foundation

The actual source APIs are `shared.providers.controller.Provider` and the provider-owned models, adapters, fixture index, schema and in-memory image helpers. There is no SDK/HTTP client, credential loader or live mode. Injected adapters exercise synthetic payload contracts against the real SQLite ledger. They do not establish model/account access, token-count/billing proof, genuine SDK retry settings or provider quality/latency.

## Required bindings and actual allocation

`Provider.run(request, *, purpose, ledger, budget, context, limits, allocation)` and `complete(messages, schema=None, *, model, purpose, ledger, budget, context, limits, allocation, max_output_tokens=512, stream=False, reasoning_effort=None, temperature=None)` require every accounting binding. The wrapper forwards the same context and allocation. There is no default purpose, global ledger, key or hidden client. `Provider.admit_operation(plan, *, ledger, budget, context, limits)` delegates whole-plan admission to the real ledger before any attempt; the mode follows the explicitly configured backend.

`prepare` validates the named model/capabilities and returns separate inference-input, semantic request/context/config, and actual serialized adapter payload hashes. Native question/option order and nonces remain in identity. Ephemeral execution IDs and local image references do not. The legacy wire model's `ExecutionEnvelope.dispatched_envelope_sha256` hashes its wire representation; the controller's `PreparedRequest.dispatched_envelope_sha256` identifies the actual adapter JSON bytes used by `RequestEvidence`. These distinct byte representations must not be substituted for each other.

The ledger's new `validate_allocation(allocation, *, context, limits, request, require_zero_dispatch=False)` returns a frozen `AdmissionView` from persisted state. It changes no holds/counters/events and is observation, not authorization. `begin_attempt(..., caller_limits=None)` rechecks inside its write transaction; after a successful transfer, tighter child attempt/repair bounds and paid cumulative outbound ceilings cannot be enlarged by later calls or restart. A stricter retroactive operation duration or concurrency schedule is explicitly refused as `strict_limits_unsupported`; admit those limits at the start. Unused holds remain until the existing completion/no-dispatch proof permits release. The SQLite version1-to-version2 migration preserves existing liabilities, policies and attempted counters.

Each injected attempt transfers one hold before one `send(payload_json, timeout_s=..., max_retries=0, max_response_bytes=...)` call. Retryable transport status handling stays inside the caller's persisted attempt cap and remaining deadline. Invalid structured output/refusal does not trigger hidden content repair. Backoff exceeding headroom stops. Usage for failed attempts still settles or retains unknown liability. An injected callable's timeout is cooperative; real SDK cancellation/retry behavior remains an installed-source testing gate. Lost response without any observed body leaves conservative liability and a closed `unknown_dispatch` exception; no fictitious capture is supplied.

## S6 strict fixture/replay seam

Use mode `strict_replay`, capture mode `fixture_replay`, a concrete reviewed immutable `FixtureIndex`, and an actually admitted offline plan whose child has max/remaining/used outbound attempts all zero. Pass `Limits.max_outbound_attempts=0` explicitly. `Provider.validate_replay_allocation` takes the same required kwargs as `run` and performs the read-only actual-ledger check before lookup. `record_reuse(..., caller_limits=...)` revalidates the zero-dispatch binding atomically after lookup. Validation is never a lease; a conflicting completion can still refuse the later write.

Lookup matches semantic request, actual payload digest, namespace, generation and public context. Changing nonce/options/purpose/source cannot reuse an old capture as a fresh observation. A miss produces `status=cache_miss`, no source capture/reported model/usable output, no attempt, no fallback transport and current external cost zero. The controller establishes this from the actual offline allocation, not an empty ID list or arbitrary stub flag. The wire validator alone cannot establish it.

Authored synthetic captures return `origin=mock`, including through the strict lookup backend. They never become recorded-live observations because a flag/nonce says replay. An observed-live record needs a trusted reviewed receipt matching its source-reference and capture hashes; none is established by this run's synthetic fixtures. Source requested/reported models, cost/usage/price and original timing remain distinct from current lookup charge/timing. Unknown original values stay unknown. No implicit payload store exists. The optional `put_safe_projection` hook passes only closed metadata to a caller-owned atomic generation-checking retention implementation; domain cache/deletion behavior is not supplied here.

## Payload and image boundaries

The [OpenAI structured-output guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=responses) distinguishes Responses `text.format` from Chat Completions `response_format` and describes refusal/incomplete outcomes. The adapters select an explicit flavor, disable tools, request strict closed output, and validate a deliberately small local schema subset. Unsupported schema features fail before dispatch rather than silently weakening validation. The [Luna model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna) documents image input, text output and structured output; it does not establish this account's access. The Python reference URL was unavailable during the initial documentation read, and no installed-client behavior was inferred from that failure.

The [TypeSafe API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) keeps one named question map and native Choice/Noul/Score results. This adapter preserves structured criteria, fractional zero-based Score/string legends, actual reported model and exact answer IDs. Both distributions must sum to one within 1e-6 without normalization. Its [retry documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/retries) documents `RetryPolicy.max_retries=0`; passing zero to a test spy is not installed-SDK proof. The [Anthropic Messages reference](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages/create) supplies the separately implemented offline system/messages/output-format and cache-usage shape. No live Anthropic grant is implied.

Images are explicit caller-supplied immutable bytes. The small decoder validates bounded noninterlaced 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNG structure, CRCs, geometry, bounded decompression and the content hash, and uses those same bytes in a payload. It never opens an image path or URL. Other formats/chunks need a separate verified decoder; rendition/source/transform provenance still belongs to the trusted caller. Actual paid image token/detail bounds are unestablished, so injected-dispatch execution refuses that capability rather than deriving tokens from byte size. Pure image payload construction and offline fixture validation do not establish paid image support.

Default persistence is metadata-only. Request/response/body/header/error canaries must not enter SQLite/WAL/JSONL, and positive-control leaks are tested. First-output timing is unavailable unless an injected observation is supplied and consistent with elapsed time; completion duration is not substituted for TTFT. All current payload/capture tests are authored synthetic controls, not real model observations or finished-app acceptance.
